model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route): NI to common less CET1 retention, net debt zero

inputs.share_count_basis: 3,024.0M common shares on the Q2-26 10-Q cover (2026-07-17) + 30.6M dilutive stock-based awards (Q2-26 diluted EPS table, treasury-stock method) = 3,054.6M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flow and buybacks are value-neutral. Series L convertible preferred (25.3M if-converted, anti-dilutive) is preferred equity whose dividend is removed inside the flow, not counted here.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 2026-06-30 = FY2025 10-K ShareBasedCompensation 1,476 - H1-25 965 + H1-26 1,033 (Q2-26 10-Q statement of changes in equity, APIC 'Stock-based compensation'). Equity-award withholding is not added on top: GAAP expense already carries the full grant value and net settlement substitutes cash for shares.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM to 2026-06-30 repurchases $18.0B (FY25 17,516 - H1-25 6,516 + H1-26 7,015) plus common dividends $5.6B = $23.6B returned vs $21.6B NI to common: WFC has been running CET1 down from 11.13% (Q2-25) to 10.26%. Repurchaser: the flat count is funded.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 10.0% in USD: 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.1 x 5.25% ERP = ~10.0%, matching the USB precedent (10.0%) and a shade below TFC (10.5%, higher-beta and smaller franchise). One rate across all three scenarios: risk is carried in the bear path and weight, not in a per-scenario premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: bank FCFE flow is after all operating costs including occupancy; no lease adjustment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Inside the flow. 'ebitda' = pre-tax income + SBC - pre-tax equivalent of (preferred dividends + NCI), so the flow is NI to COMMON. Preferred par is therefore NOT also deducted in the bridge (USB convention, not TFC/HBAN). TTM pref dividends 995, NCI 357 (inflated by Q2-26 venture-gain NCI of 238).
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, net_debt = 0. SKILL.md routes banks to residual income on tangible book; the house precedent for large US banks (USB, TFC, HBAN, NTRS, STT) is FCFE-at-CoE on the engine route, which is the same economics (value = TCE + PV of returns above CoE) expressed as distributable cash, and keeps WFC comparable to those names. Deposits are operating funding, not debt; OCF is meaningless for a bank (CSV OCF swings -19.0B to +40.4B). Engine mapping: revenue = NII + noninterest income (GAAP; CSV Revenue column is a mis-tagged fee subset, unused) from SEC companyfacts, TTM to 2026-06-30: NII 48,694 + nonII 38,102 = 86,796. 'ebitda' = pre-tax 27,463 + SBC 1,544 - (pref 995 + NCI 357)/(1 - 16.4% ETR) 1,617 = 27,390 (31.6% margin). sbc_pct removes SBC; D&A 0 (inside opex); cash tax on the remainder; 'capex' = CET1 retention needed to hold the CET1/revenue ratio (137,698/86,796 = 1.586) as revenue grows: capex% = 158.6 x g/(1+g). FY0 check: (27,390 - 1,544) x (1 - 16.4%) = 21,607 vs reported NI to common 21,615. CET1 10.26% vs 8.50% regulatory minimum+buffers: the ~175bp cushion is a normal operating buffer for a GSIB (management has drawn it down from 11.1% via buybacks), so NO excess-capital credit is put in the bridge. AOCI is already in standardized CET1 (Category I GSIB). FY0 is TTM to June so flows start at the balance-sheet and share-count dates; the TTM still contains seasonal Q1 comp expense and Q3/Q4-25 pre-cap-lift quarters, which is why year 1 margin steps up toward FY26 guidance (NII ~$50B, expense ~$55.7B -> implied H2-26 pre-tax margin ~35%).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~0%) diverges far more than 30% from revenue (4.0%) and EPS (24.3%) CAGRs. Book value was held flat by $73B of buybacks FY2022-25 under the asset cap, and EPS growth is buyback- and recovery-driven off a 2022 trough. 5-year EPS and FCF CAGRs start at the FY2020 COVID-provision trough (EPS $0.42) and are meaningless. Revenue is the selected anchor (Visa/USB precedent for heavy repurchasers).
historical_growth.notes: FCF here is the bank owner-flow proxy: NI to common (SBC is already a GAAP expense). Revenue history is not smooth: FY2020-22 NII collapsed with zero rates, FY2021 nonII includes venture/equity-securities gains and FY2023 NII was the rate peak. The asset cap held the balance sheet at ~$1.95T from 2018 to June 2025; assets are now $2.28T.

base.margin_rationale: Year 1 34.0% sits just below the ~35% implied by FY26 guidance for H2-26 (NII ~$50B, expense ~$55.7B, provisions ~$2B/half). Fades to 33.3% as provisions normalise from 0.37% of loans toward a through-cycle ~0.5%. Terminal ROTCE ~16% on CET1/revenue 1.59: below the 17-18% medium-term target, which is a good-year number.
base.capex_rationale: CET1 retention = 1.586 x g/(1+g): holds the CET1 ratio at today's 10.26% as RWA grows with revenue.
base.tax_rationale: Underlying ETR ~17-18% (Q2-26 17.4%; H1 14.9% had discrete benefits). Ramps to 20% as OBBBA phases out renewable-energy credits that currently shelter income.

bull.margin_rationale: Efficiency ratio keeps falling from ~60% toward the mid-50s as CIB and Wealth scale; terminal ROTCE ~17.5%, inside the 17-18% target sustained.

bear.margin_rationale: NIM compression holds year-1 margin at the TTM level; a credit cycle (CRE office/multifamily plus consumer) lifts provisions to ~1% of loans in year 2, roughly $7B above base; recovery to a 30.5% margin, terminal ROTCE ~14%.

scenario_narratives.base: The post-asset-cap growth phase runs for two to three years and then fades. Loans grow mid-to-high single digits as WFC re-levers its balance sheet into a deposit franchise that holds ~10% of US deposits, and NIM settles in the low-2.4s. Expenses stay near $56-57B, so the efficiency ratio drifts toward the high 50s. Credit normalises from today's 0.37% charge toward ~0.5% through the cycle. ROTCE runs ~16-17%, just below management's 17-18% target, and roughly two-thirds of earnings are distributed while the rest funds CET1 to keep the ratio at 10.3%.
scenario_narratives.bull: With the asset cap gone and the consent orders cleared, WFC becomes a share-gainer. CIB and Markets close part of the gap to the bulge bracket (record IB fees, markets revenue +24% in Q2-26), loans compound at 7-8% for two years, and NIM stabilises in H2-26 as management guided. Final 2026-27 capital rules (eSLR and Basel endgame re-proposal) are benign, so retention stays modest. The efficiency ratio falls into the mid-50s and ROTCE holds at 17.5-18.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: NIM keeps compressing as deposit costs stay sticky into rate cuts, and the CIB push adds risk faster than it adds returns. A credit cycle concentrated in CRE (nonperforming apartment loans are rising, plus office) and in consumer cards drives provisions to ~1% of loans in year 2. Revenue growth stalls at 2-3%, the tax shelter from renewable credits disappears, and ROTCE settles at ~14%. A renewed compliance lapse, the residual governance risk, would also put a cap back on growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%. Late-cycle CRE and consumer credit, a NIM still compressing, and a print where the stock fell on a beat make the downside a live path, not a tail. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things at once: CIB scaling without a risk event, NIM stabilising, and benign capital rules. Base keeps 50%, anchored on reaffirmed FY26 guidance and ROTCE already inside the target range. Same 25/50/25 as the TFC precedent.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on what it can pay its common shareholders after funding the capital its growth requires: NI to common less the CET1 retention that keeps the ratio constant, discounted at the cost of equity. Deposits are funding, not debt, so nothing is deducted for net debt. Preferred dividends and NCI are taken out inside the flow. The value is therefore TCE plus the PV of returns above the 10% cost of equity. At a through-cycle ROTCE of ~16% WFC earns a ~6pt spread, which justifies roughly 1.8-1.9x tangible book. The stock trades at 1.74x TBVPS of $46.13.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit: base assumes provisions normalise to ~0.5% of loans; a CRE- or consumer-led cycle at 1%+ for two years is the bear path.
NIM: every 10bp on ~$2.0T of earning assets is ~$2B of pre-tax income, about 2.3pts of margin.
Capital rules: final eSLR and Basel III endgame calibration set the CET1 the growth has to carry. Retention is modelled at today's 10.26%; a 50bp higher requirement costs ~$6.7B up front.
Tax: the ~17-18% ETR depends on tax-credit investments; the path ramps to 20% but a faster loss of credits would cut about 1% of value per point.
Execution and governance: CIB expansion risk, and the chance of a renewed regulatory constraint after the consent orders were lifted.
